- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish — apply downward correction in next 5-7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust downward quickly — apply lagged correction: reduce forecast by 1-2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >+10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1-3% per day; if below -10%, increase by 1-3% per day.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 in 3 consecutive days → model overfits noise → reduce forecast volatility by 10-20% in next 7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and price is trending, model often misses direction — align forecast with sentiment’s direction, not just price momentum.
